  - Additional typed `RegExp.escape(text)` coverage is implemented for literal-pattern escaping. Test: `regexp_escape`.
  - Additional typed Map/Set constructor coverage is implemented for `new Set(valuesArray)` and `new Map(Object.entries(obj))` over string-key entry arrays. Test: `map_set_constructors`.
  - Additional collection own-property helper coverage is implemented for empty `Object.keys` / `Object.values` / `Object.entries` / `Object.getOwnPropertyNames` / `Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor(s)` / `Object.hasOwn` / inherited `hasOwnProperty` / `propertyIsEnumerable` / `Reflect.ownKeys` / `Reflect.getOwnPropertyDescriptor` results on `Map`, `Set`, `WeakMap`, `WeakSet`, `WeakRef`, and `FinalizationRegistry` instances. Test: `collection_object_methods`.
  - Additional typed Map/Set numeric key coverage is implemented for SameValueZero `NaN` matching and `-0`/`0` coalescing. Test: `map_set_same_value_zero`.
  - Additional typed `Array.prototype.flatMap()` coverage is implemented for scalar callback results as well as array callback results. Test: `array_flat`.
  - Additional typed array higher-order callback coverage is implemented for the standard receiver array argument across inline expression/single-return-block callbacks, direct function references, and closure callback values; typed `find` / `findLast` return `undefined` when no element matches for element types that can flow through `tsc_value_t`, including inferred numeric/boolean nullish locals assigned from the result. Tests: `array_hof`, `array_find_last`.
  - Additional dynamic array higher-order callback coverage is implemented for the standard receiver array argument across inline expression/single-return-block callbacks, direct function references, closure callback values, and `reduce`/`reduceRight`. Tests: `dynamic_array_hof`, `dynamic_array_hof_refs`.
  - Additional typed and dynamic array higher-order `thisArg` coverage is implemented for optional `thisArg` evaluation and binding into direct/inline callbacks that declare `this: any`. Test: `array_hof_this_arg`.
  - Additional typed and dynamic string-pattern coverage is implemented for `match("pattern")` and `matchAll("pattern")`. Tests: `string_match_string`, `dynamic_string_match_string`.
  - Additional typed and dynamic string-pattern coverage is implemented for `search("pattern")`. Tests: `string_search_string`, `dynamic_string_search`.
  - Additional static `Reflect.apply`/`Reflect.construct` coverage is implemented for typed-array, dynamic-array, and array-literal-spread argument lists, with runtime arity mismatches routed through catchable exceptions. Tests: `reflect_apply`, `reflect_construct`, `reflect_length_errors`.
  - Additional typed array property-name coverage is implemented for `Object.getOwnPropertyNames(array)` and `Reflect.ownKeys(array)`. Test: `object_array_enumeration`.
  - Additional typed and dynamic `Array.prototype.entries()` coverage is implemented as materialized `[string, value]` entry arrays. Tests: `array_entries`, `dynamic_array_entries`.
  - Additional typed `Array.prototype.concat()` coverage is implemented for spread elements inside array-literal arguments. Test: `array_concat_values`.
  - Additional dynamic array-literal spread coverage is implemented for dynamic arrays, dynamic/typed strings, and typed arrays. Test: `dynamic_array_spread`.
  - Additional dynamic array string-key write and `length` write coverage is implemented for `arr["1"] = value` and `Reflect.set`. Test: `dynamic_array_property_writes`.
  - Additional dynamic array HOF callback-reference coverage is implemented for named callbacks with declared parameter coercion. Test: `dynamic_array_hof_refs`.
  - Additional bounded dynamic array `defineProperty` coverage is implemented for dense indexes and `length`. Test: `dynamic_array_define_property`.
  - Additional typed Map/Set `forEach` coverage is implemented for single-return block-body inline callbacks and named callback references with value/key-or-value2/receiver parameters, plus optional `thisArg` evaluation and binding for callbacks that declare `this: any`. Tests: `map_set_for_each`, `map_set_for_each_refs`, `map_set_for_each_this_arg`.
  - Additional dynamic accessor descriptor coverage is implemented for function-scope closure-valued getters/setters and inline closure expressions. Test: `object_accessor_closures`.
  - Additional configurable accessor descriptor redefinition coverage is implemented for omitted hook/flag preservation and explicit undefined hook clearing. Test: `object_accessor_preserve`.
  - Additional dynamic `Object.defineProperties` coverage is implemented for static descriptor maps containing data and closure-valued accessor descriptors. Test: `object_define_properties`.
  - Additional dynamic `Object.create(proto, descriptors)` coverage is implemented for static descriptor maps on newly created prototype-linked objects. Test: `object_create_descriptors`.
  - Additional descriptor-default coverage is implemented for omitted data `value` defaults, explicit undefined accessor hooks, and own undefined `get`/`set` fields for absent accessor hooks. Test: `object_descriptor_defaults`.
  - Additional descriptor kind-transition coverage is implemented for configurable data-to-accessor/accessor-to-data redefinitions and non-configurable data-to-accessor rejection. Test: `object_descriptor_kind_transition`.
  - Additional descriptor object-literal coverage is implemented for shorthand fields, shorthand accessor identifiers, and boolean flag expressions. Test: `object_descriptor_shorthand`.
  - Additional data descriptor redefinition coverage is implemented for omitted-field preservation, compatible non-configurable writable updates, and incompatible flag/value changes. Test: `object_descriptor_redefine`.
  - Additional accessor descriptor redefinition coverage is implemented for compatible non-configurable getter/setter identity preservation and incompatible flag/accessor changes. Test: `object_accessor_redefine`.
  - Additional bounded dynamic array extensibility coverage is implemented for `Object.preventExtensions`, `Object.seal`, `Object.freeze`, Reflect/Object index writes, dense-index definitions, index/length descriptor flags, `length` writes, deletion checks, and core mutator-method guards. Primitive Object extensibility and empty own-property helpers are implemented for non-object values, including empty key/value/entry enumeration for non-string primitives. Tests: `dynamic_array_extensibility`, `object_primitive_extensibility`.
  - Additional receiver-bound accessor coverage is implemented for direct, lifted, and closure-valued accessor functions with a TypeScript `this: any` parameter. Test: `reflect_receiver`.
  - Additional accessor descriptor identity coverage is implemented for stable boxed `get`/`set` function identities across repeated `Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor` reads, including `typeof`, `String(...)`, `Object.is`, and `===`. Test: `reflect_receiver`.
  - Additional dynamic `Reflect.apply` coverage is implemented for invoking boxed accessor descriptor `get`/`set` identities with a supplied receiver. Test: `reflect_receiver`.
  - Additional typed `Reflect.get(target, key, receiver)` coverage is implemented for optional receiver evaluation on typed arrays, typed interface/class objects, and Buffer data-property reads. Test: `reflect_get_receiver_typed`.
  - Additional `Reflect.apply` coverage is implemented for binding `thisArg` into function values that declare `this: any`. Test: `reflect_apply`.
  - Still missing: hidden classes / shape trees, inline caches and diagnostics, complete built-in object/array prototype behavior, broader prototype method coverage, and remaining descriptor/prototype edge cases.
  - Still blocks: production-quality untyped npm packages, remaining `Proxy` construct/invariant coverage, full `Reflect`, remaining property descriptor edge cases, and high-performance dynamic property access.

---

## 2. Medium-term phases (weeks each)

- **Phase 6 — `async`/`await` + libuv event loop** (~3 weeks)
  - Settled/immediate `Promise<T>` values are implemented for `Promise.resolve(value)`, `Promise.reject(reason)`, synchronous `.then(...)`, `.catch(...)`, `.finally(...)`, and settled-array `Promise.all`/`allSettled`/`race`/`any` over compiler-known callbacks and promise arrays. Test: `promise_settled`
  - `new Promise<T>(executor)` now supports an immediate/synchronous subset: the executor is called once, generated `resolve` / `reject` callbacks settle at most once, executor throws become rejections unless already settled, and executors that do not settle return a pending promise. Test: `promise_executor`
  - `Promise.resolve(existingPromise)` now adopts an existing native Promise record, preserving fulfilled, rejected, and pending state. Test: `promise_resolve_adopt`
  - `Promise.try(callback)` is implemented for immediate callbacks, fulfilling from returned values and rejecting from thrown values. Test: `promise_try`
  - `Promise.prototype.then()` now accepts an omitted fulfillment handler and `.then(undefined, onRejected)` in the immediate subset, passing fulfilled values through while preserving rejection handling. Test: `promise_then_passthrough`
  - `Promise.prototype.catch()` and `.finally()` now accept omitted or `undefined` handlers in the immediate subset, preserving fulfilled, rejected, and pending state. Test: `promise_empty_handlers`
  - Immediate Promise callbacks and `Promise.try(callback)` now adopt returned native Promise records instead of boxing them as fulfillment values. Test: `promise_callback_adopt`
  - Immediate `.finally()` callbacks now adopt returned native Promise records for rejected and pending outcomes while preserving the original promise state after fulfilled returned promises. Test: `promise_finally_adopt`
  - Immediate `.then` / `.catch` / `.finally` callback throws now become rejected Promise records in the same synchronous subset. Test: `promise_callback_throw`
  - Top-level `async function` declarations, class `async` methods, and async function values without `await` return immediate Promise records: returned values fulfill, returned native Promise records are adopted, implicit returns fulfill with `undefined`, and synchronous uncaught throws reject. Tests: `async_function_immediate`, `async_methods_immediate`, `async_function_values_immediate`, `async_throw_rejection`
  - Immediate `await` over native Promise records and non-Promise values is implemented inside the current async subset: fulfilled awaits unwrap values, non-Promise awaits evaluate once and continue with that value, rejected awaits return rejected Promise records, and pending awaits return pending Promise records without scheduling a continuation. Tests: `async_await_immediate`, `async_await_values_immediate`
  - Local `try`/`catch` inside the immediate async subset catches rejected native Promise records from `await`; uncaught awaited rejections still return rejected Promise records. Test: `async_await_try_catch`
  - Full state-machine lowering of each `async` function remains deferred. A real `await` must become a suspend/resume point that chains a `.then` onto the awaited promise.
  - `Promise.any` now rejects with an AggregateError-shaped dynamic object containing `name`, `message`, and `errors` when every input rejects, including empty input. Test: `promise_any_aggregate`
  - Empty `Promise.race([])` now returns a pending promise whose chained `.then` / `.catch` / `.finally` callbacks are not synchronously invoked. Test: `promise_race_empty_pending`
  - Pending records now propagate through immediate `Promise.all` / `allSettled` / `race` / `any` without synchronously invoking chained callbacks. Test: `promise_pending_combinators`
  - Still missing: suspend/resume `await` state-machine lowering, microtask-scheduled `.then` dispatch, arbitrary thenable assimilation, and full async function edge cases.
  - Full Promise microtask scheduling plus full `process.nextTick` scheduling remains; a bounded `process.nextTick(callback, ...args)` queue is implemented for up to three typed callback arguments, a bounded `queueMicrotask(callback)` queue is implemented for zero-argument callbacks drained after next ticks, a bounded zero-delay `setTimeout(callback, 0, ...args)` queue is implemented for up to three typed callback arguments plus explicit `undefined` / `void 0` omitted-delay and `-0` forms drained after next ticks and microtasks with numeric handles cancellable by `clearTimeout(handle)` / `clearInterval(handle)` before drain, and a bounded `setImmediate(callback, ...args)` queue is implemented for up to three typed callback arguments drained after next ticks, microtasks, and zero-delay timeouts before program exit with numeric handles cancellable by `clearImmediate(handle)` before drain; scheduler callbacks with explicit `this: any` parameters receive runtime `undefined`, and omitted or undefined-valued clear handles are no-op clears that preserve argument side effects. Tests: `queue_microtask`, `set_timeout_zero`, `set_immediate`, `timers_clear`, `scheduler_callback_this`
  - libuv (`libuv1-dev`) bound for nonzero-delay `setTimeout`, `setInterval`, real event-loop-backed `setImmediate`, and all future async I/O.
  - **Depends on Phase 3** for the `Promise<T>` value representation (mixed boxed + unboxed).

- **Phase 7 remainder — ES language features** (~3 weeks)
  - Synchronous `function*` declarations with ordinary `yield expr` statements, bounded `yield*` over arrays, strings, or dynamic iterable values, and materialized `.next(value?)` / `.return(value)` / `.throw(error)` cursor interactions are implemented as eager materialized `Iterator<T>` / `IterableIterator<T>` arrays. Optional `.next(value)` inputs are evaluated and ignored in the eager subset. Tests: `generator_functions`, `generator_next_argument`
  - Still missing: lazy generator state-machine lowering with suspend/resume semantics, bidirectional `.next(value)` into suspended `yield`, non-eager side-effect timing, and `async function*`.
  - `FinalizationRegistry<T>` is implemented with `.register(target, heldValue, unregisterToken?)`, `.unregister(unregisterToken)`, and `[object FinalizationRegistry]` stringification; the cleanup callback is accepted by the constructor but never invoked because this AOT runtime has no GC-finalizer plumbing. Test: `finalization_registry`
  - `String.raw` tagged templates are implemented for raw segment preservation with stringified substitutions. Test: `string_raw`
  - Array-backed custom iterable classes, class iterator objects with direct or inherited `next()`, direct self-iterable iterator objects, and `ObjectEntry<T>` destructuring over custom iterators are implemented. Tests: `custom_iterable`, `custom_iterator_object`, `custom_iterator_inherited_next`, `custom_iterator_self`, `custom_iterator_entry_destructure`
  - Broader iterator protocol edge cases remain, including lazy generator-backed iterables and async iterables.

- **Phase 9 — `Proxy` + `Reflect`** (~2 weeks)
  - `Proxy` object traps for `get`, `set`, `has`, `deleteProperty`, `defineProperty`, `getOwnPropertyDescriptor`, `ownKeys`, `getPrototypeOf`, `setPrototypeOf`, `isExtensible`, and `preventExtensions` are implemented for dynamic objects, including `Object.keys(proxy)` filtering trapped `ownKeys` through descriptor enumerability. Non-nullish object trap values must be callable before dispatch, while callable proxy-valued traps still forward correctly; `ownKeys` trap result validation rejects duplicate keys, missing non-configurable target keys, non-array results, non-string entries, and non-extensible target key mismatches; `getOwnPropertyDescriptor` trap result validation rejects invalid result types, hidden non-configurable keys, hidden or invented keys on non-extensible targets, invalid non-configurable descriptor claims, descriptor-kind mismatches, changed non-configurable enumerable flags, changed fixed data values, and changed fixed accessor getter/setter identities; `get`, `set`, and `defineProperty` trap result validation rejects fixed-data/accessor violations, fixed accessor getter/setter identity changes, additions to non-extensible targets, and invalid non-configurable descriptor claims; accessor `defineProperty` descriptors route through proxy traps and fallback target definitions; `has` and `deleteProperty` trap result validation rejects false/deleted results that would hide or remove non-configurable keys or existing keys on non-extensible targets; prototype/extensibility trap validation rejects invalid or inconsistent `getPrototypeOf`, `setPrototypeOf`, `isExtensible`, and `preventExtensions` results, while `Object.setPrototypeOf` rejects invalid prototype values before proxy trap dispatch and throws on falsy proxy setPrototypeOf trap results. Function `apply` traps are implemented through dynamic `Reflect.apply`, direct dynamic calls, and dynamic object method calls, construct traps are implemented through dynamic `Reflect.construct(proxyCtor, args)` and direct dynamic `new` calls over identifier or property-access constructor values, and object-target proxies cannot become callable or constructable through traps. Function-target proxies preserve callable/constructable `typeof` identity including nested proxies and after revocation, dynamic `Reflect.apply` validates targets and accepts array/array-like argument lists before proxy trap dispatch, direct dynamic calls and dynamic method calls validate and forward callable proxies, dynamic `Reflect.construct` validates targets, accepts array/array-like argument lists, validates explicit `newTarget` values before proxy trap dispatch, and accepts object/array/function construct-trap results while rejecting primitive results, and direct dynamic `new` validates and forwards constructable proxies. Nested callable proxies preserve stringification and JSON function omission/null behavior, `Object.prototype.toString.call(proxy)` reports callable proxy chains as `[object Function]`, array targets are accepted by `new Proxy(...)` / `Proxy.revocable(...)`, and nested array proxies preserve `Array.isArray(...)` identity, `Object.prototype.toString.call(proxy)` `[object Array]` tags, dynamic `.length` reads, trapless Object/Reflect own-key, value, entry, descriptor, `has`, and enumerability helper forwarding, trapless dynamic writes, `Reflect.set`, descriptor definitions, length updates, and deletes forwarding, and trapless prototype/extensibility checks plus `Reflect.getPrototypeOf`, `Reflect.setPrototypeOf`, `Reflect.preventExtensions`, `Object.getPrototypeOf`, `Object.setPrototypeOf`, `Object.seal`, `Object.freeze`, `Object.isSealed`, and `Object.isFrozen` forwarding, and array-target `getPrototypeOf`/`setPrototypeOf`, function-target `isExtensible`/`preventExtensions` extensibility-trap checks, and array-target `isExtensible`/`preventExtensions`, `ownKeys`, `getOwnPropertyDescriptor`, `defineProperty`, `get`, `set`, `has`, and `deleteProperty` trap invariant checks. Nested revoked callable proxies preserve `typeof` identity while throwing revoked-get errors for `String(...)` and `JSON.stringify(...)`, and revoked array proxies reject `Array.isArray(...)`. Revoked proxies throw through direct calls, method calls, direct `new` calls, `Reflect.apply`, `Reflect.construct`, `String(proxy)`, `Object.prototype.toString.call(proxy)`, and `JSON.stringify(proxy)`. Tests: `proxy`, `proxy-ownkeys`, `proxy_traps`, `proxy_callable_identity`, `proxy_callable_to_string_tag`, `proxy_apply_forward`, `proxy_array_mutation_forward`, `proxy_array_extensibility_forward`, `proxy_array_seal_freeze_forward`, `proxy_array_extensibility_trap_invariants`, `proxy_array_ownkeys_invariants`, `proxy_array_descriptor_invariants`, `proxy_array_define_invariants`, `proxy_array_get_set_invariants`, `proxy_array_has_delete_invariants`, `proxy_array_object_helpers`, `proxy_array_is_array`, `proxy_array_prototype_invariants`, `proxy_array_to_string_tag`, `proxy_direct_call`, `proxy_method_call`, `proxy_direct_construct`, `reflect_apply_validation`, `reflect_arguments_array_like`, `proxy_callable_target_validation`, `proxy_callable_trap_validation`, `proxy_object_trap_callable_validation`, `proxy_define_accessor`, `proxy_nested_callable_identity`, `proxy_callable_string`, `proxy_callable_json`, `proxy_construct_forward`, `proxy_construct_new_target`, `proxy_construct_return_objects`, `reflect_construct_validation`, `reflect_construct_new_target_validation`, `proxy_revocable_callable`, `proxy_revocable_identity`, `proxy_constructor_validation`, `proxy_ownkeys_result_validation`, `proxy_ownkeys_entry_validation`, `proxy_ownkeys_invariants`, `proxy_descriptor_invariants`, `proxy_get_set_define_invariants`, `proxy_has_delete_invariants`, `proxy_prototype_extensibility_invariants`, `object_set_prototype_of_validation`, `proxy_construct`.
  - Still missing: broader proxy callable/newable identity edge cases beyond the covered `typeof` / `Object.prototype.toString.call(...)` for callable and array proxies / nested callable identity / array-proxy `Array.isArray(...)` identity / `Reflect.apply` forwarding / direct dynamic calls / dynamic object method calls / callable target/trap validation / object-trap callability / `String(...)` / JSON omission / construct forwarding / direct dynamic `new` / explicit `newTarget` forwarding / revoked callable identity paths, and broader ECMAScript proxy edge-case validation beyond constructor input and current result/invariant validation.
  - `Reflect.*` API; dynamic `Reflect.get`/`Reflect.set`/`Reflect.has`/`Reflect.deleteProperty`/`Reflect.ownKeys`/`Reflect.defineProperty`/`Reflect.getPrototypeOf`/`Reflect.setPrototypeOf`/`Reflect.getOwnPropertyDescriptor`/`Reflect.isExtensible`/`Reflect.preventExtensions` are implemented, dynamic get/set accept receiver arguments for data/accessor dispatch, dynamic `Reflect.apply` can invoke boxed accessor descriptor functions while accepting array-like argument lists and reporting catchable target/argument-list validation errors, dynamic `Reflect.construct` accepts array-like argument lists and reports catchable target/newTarget/argument-list validation errors, dynamic property/prototype/extensibility helpers reject non-object targets, and bounded static `Reflect.apply`/`Reflect.construct` over known function/class values accepts array-literal, array-literal-spread, typed-array, and dynamic-array argument lists. Test: `reflect_property_target_validation`.
  - `Object.defineProperty` with full property descriptor semantics; dynamic data descriptors enforce `writable`/`configurable`/`enumerable`, named-function, lifted-arrow/function-expression, and closure-valued accessors work, accessors can observe receiver-bound `this` through `this: any`, descriptor `get`/`set` values expose stable boxed function identities, and those boxed accessor identities are callable through dynamic `Reflect.apply`
  - **Depends on Phase 3** heavily — proxies intercept dynamic property access.

---

## 3. Long-term phases (months)

- **Phases 11–13 — async Node stdlib** (~2 months total)
  - Phase 11: synchronous `EventEmitter` is implemented as a global constructor, named import, and namespace import from `"events"` / `"node:events"` with `on`/`addListener`/`prependListener`/`once`/`prependOnceListener`/`off`/`removeListener`/`removeAllListeners`/`emit`/`listenerCount(eventName, listener?)`/`listeners(eventName)`/`rawListeners(eventName)`/`eventNames(...ignored)`/`setMaxListeners`/`getMaxListeners(...ignored)` plus module-level `events.listenerCount(emitter, eventName, listener?)`/`getEventListeners`/`events.once(emitter, eventName)`/`setMaxListeners`/`getMaxListeners` and static `EventEmitter.listenerCount(emitter, eventName, listener?)` plus `EventEmitter.defaultMaxListeners` / `events.defaultMaxListeners` for string event names and typed listeners. Listener callbacks with explicit `this: EventEmitter` parameters receive the emitting instance. Listener inspection returns stable boxed function identities suitable for `typeof`, stringification, `Object.is`, and strict equality checks; `rawListeners` exposes stable once-wrapper identities with `.listener` back-pointers. `events.once(...)` returns a Promise fulfilled by the next matching synchronous `emit` with an array of emitted args, or rejected by an intervening `"error"` event. The default listener limit is shared across global/module/static reads and applies to emitters without an own `setMaxListeners(...)` value. Unhandled `"error"` emits throw when no listener is registered, duplicate listener removal removes the most recently added matching listener, and once listeners are removed before invocation for reentrant emits. Synchronous global `Event` / `EventTarget` construction is also implemented for typed listeners, duplicate listener suppression, removal by identity, same-target dispatch, listener callbacks with explicit `this: EventTarget` receiving the dispatch target, literal `{ once }`/`capture`/`passive` listener options with once removal before invocation, `type`/`target`/`currentTarget`/`defaultPrevented`/`cancelable`, cancelable `{ cancelable: true }` events, `new EventTarget(...ignored)`, and `preventDefault(...ignored)`. Event no-op compatibility also evaluates and ignores extras for `new EventEmitter(...)` / `new events.EventEmitter(...)`. Process metadata methods now evaluate and ignore extra arguments where JavaScript ignores them for `cwd`, `uptime`, `hrtime`, `hrtime.bigint`, POSIX id/group reads, `umask(mask)`, `memoryUsage`, and `resourceUsage`; no-option `os` metadata methods do the same for `platform`, `type`, `release`, `version`, `endianness`, `machine`, `arch`, `hostname`, `tmpdir`, `homedir`, `cpus`, `availableParallelism`, `totalmem`, `freemem`, `uptime`, and `loadavg`. Tests: `event_emitter`, `event_emitter_import`, `event_emitter_more`, `event_emitter_namespace`, `event_emitter_max_listeners`, `event_emitter_default_max_listeners`, `event_emitter_listener_count_filter`, `event_emitter_error_event`, `event_emitter_remove_latest`, `event_emitter_once_reentrant`, `event_emitter_once_promise`, `event_emitter_listeners`, `event_emitter_raw_listeners`, `event_emitter_static_listener_count`, `event_emitter_this`, `event_target`, `event_target_options`, `event_target_this`, `process_metadata`, `process_hrtime`, `process_hrtime_bigint`, `process_posix_ids`, `process_getgroups`, `process_umask`, `process_memory_usage`, `process_resource_usage`, `stdlib_os`, `os_more`, `os_host_more`, `os_system_stats`
  - `fs.promises.readFile`/`writeFile`/`appendFile`/`readdir`/`stat`/`lstat`/`realpath`/`readlink`/`symlink`/`link`/`mkdtemp`/`truncate`/`utimes`/`lutimes`/`chown`/`lchown`/`chmod`/`access`/`mkdir`/`unlink`/`rm`/`rmdir`/`cp`/`copyFile`/`rename` are implemented as immediate-settled wrappers around the sync fs runtime for global `fs.promises`, named `promises` imports, and namespace imports from `"fs"` / `"node:fs"`. Sync `fs.statSync` / `node:fs.statSync` and `fs.lstatSync` / `node:fs.lstatSync` return the same small `Stats` subset with numeric metadata, timestamp fields, `isFile(...ignored)`, `isDirectory(...ignored)`, `isSymbolicLink(...ignored)`, `isBlockDevice(...ignored)`, `isCharacterDevice(...ignored)`, `isFIFO(...ignored)`, and `isSocket(...ignored)`, and accept literal `{ bigint: false }` plus `{ throwIfNoEntry: true | false }` options, with false returning / fulfilling with `undefined` for missing paths. `fs.realpathSync` / `node:fs.realpathSync` plus `fs.readlinkSync` / `node:fs.readlinkSync` / `fs.symlinkSync` / `node:fs.symlinkSync` / `fs.linkSync` / `node:fs.linkSync` resolve or create host filesystem links, with `realpath`/`readlink` accepting literal UTF-8 and explicit Buffer/null object encoding options and `symlink` accepting literal type arguments. `fs.readFileSync` and immediate `fs.promises.readFile` accept explicit `"buffer"`, `null`, `{ encoding: "buffer" }`, and `{ encoding: null }` options for Buffer results. `fs.readdirSync` / `node:fs.readdirSync` accepts explicit `"buffer"` / `{ encoding: "buffer" }` options for Buffer filename arrays, literal `{ recursive: true }` options for recursive relative string results, literal `{ encoding: "buffer", recursive: true }` for recursive relative Buffer results, and literal `{ withFileTypes: true }` options for a bounded `Dirent` subset with `name` plus the same ignored-argument POSIX kind predicates. `fs.mkdtempSync` / `node:fs.mkdtempSync` create temporary directories from a prefix and accept literal UTF-8 and explicit Buffer/null object encoding options, `fs.truncateSync` / `node:fs.truncateSync` truncates files by path, `fs.utimesSync` / `node:fs.utimesSync` updates access/modification times from numeric seconds or `Date` values, `fs.lutimesSync` / `node:fs.lutimesSync` updates symlink access/modification times without following targets, `fs.chownSync` / `node:fs.chownSync` changes numeric uid/gid ownership, `fs.lchownSync` / `node:fs.lchownSync` changes numeric uid/gid ownership on symlink paths, `fs.chmodSync` / `node:fs.chmodSync` changes numeric file modes, and `fs.accessSync` / `node:fs.accessSync` checks path accessibility with optional POSIX `fs.constants.{F_OK,R_OK,W_OK,X_OK}` mode checks. Bounded UTF-8 encoding options are implemented for read/write/append/readdir/realpath/readlink/mkdtemp, `readFile` accepts literal `{ flag: "r" | "rs" | "r+" | "rs+" }` and explicit Buffer/null encodings, `writeFile` accepts literal `{ flag: "w" | "wx" | "w+" | "wx+" | "a" | "ax" | "a+" | "ax+" | "as" | "as+" | "r+" | "rs+" }`, `appendFile` accepts literal `{ flag: "a" | "ax" | "a+" | "ax+" | "as" | "as+" }`, write/append accept numeric `{ mode }` for newly created files and literal `{ flush }` compatibility options, readdir/realpath/readlink/mkdtemp accept explicit Buffer/null object encodings plus readdir literal `{ recursive: true }` and `{ withFileTypes: true }`, write/append accept string or Buffer data, recursive and numeric mode options are implemented for `mkdir`, recursive/force options plus retry-count/delay compatibility options for `rm`, recursive plus retry-count/delay compatibility options for `rmdir`, bounded regular-file/directory/symlink copying plus `force`/`errorOnExist`/`dereference`/`verbatimSymlinks`/numeric `mode`/`preserveTimestamps` behavior is implemented for `cp`, and supported sync fs calls route from named imports. Sync filesystem throws inside these promise wrappers are converted into rejected Promise records.   - Immediate `dns.lookup(hostname, callback)`, `dns.lookup(hostname, 4|6|0, callback)`, `dns.lookup(hostname, { family, all, hints, verbatim, order }, callback)`, and `dns.promises.lookup(hostname[, 4|6|0 | { family, all, hints, verbatim, order }])` are implemented for global `dns`, named imports, named `promises` imports, and namespace imports from `"dns"` / `"node:dns"`, backed by host `getaddrinfo` and immediate delivery of error/address/family, dynamic `{ address, family }` Promise results, or `{ all: true }` arrays of dynamic result objects. `node_modules_commonjs_module_exports_object_from_entries_named`, `node_modules_commonjs_module_exports_object_from_entries_computed_named`, `node_modules_commonjs_module_exports_object_from_entries_identifier_named`, `node_modules_commonjs_module_exports_object_from_entries_require_values`, `node_modules_commonjs_module_exports_object_from_entries_object_entries_named`, `node_modules_commonjs_module_exports_object_from_entries_object_entries_identifier_named`, `node_modules_commonjs_module_exports_object_wrapper_from_entries_named`, `node_modules_commonjs_module_exports_object_wrapper_from_entries_variants_named`, `node_modules_commonjs_module_exports_object_wrapper_from_entries_object_entries_identifier_variants_named`, `node_modules_commonjs_module_exports_object_runtime_defaults`, `node_modules_commonjs_module_exports_object_wrappers_named`, `node_modules_commonjs_module_exports_object_set_prototype_named`, `node_modules_commonjs_module_exports_object_spread_named`, `node_modules_commonjs_module_exports_object_getter_named`, `node_modules_commonjs_object_spread_default`, `node_modules_commonjs_module_exports_value_chains`, `node_modules_commonjs_module_exports_object_default`, `node_modules_commonjs_module_exports_nested_object_default`, `node_modules_commonjs_module_exports_object_function`, `node_modules_commonjs_module_exports_object_arrow`, `node_modules_commonjs_module_exports_object_method`, `node_modules_commonjs_module_exports_object_literals`, `node_modules_commonjs_module_exports_function`, `node_modules_commonjs_module_exports_arrow`, `node_modules_commonjs_module_exports_identifier`, `node_modules_commonjs_module_exports_primitives`, `node_modules_commonjs_require_named`, `node_modules_commonjs_require_direct_member`, `node_modules_commonjs_require_direct_function`, `node_modules_commonjs_require_direct_value`, `node_modules_commonjs_require_destructure`, `node_modules_commonjs_require_function`, `node_modules_commonjs_relative_require`, `node_modules_commonjs_relative_require_default`, `node_modules_commonjs_relative_require_direct_default`, `node_modules_commonjs_relative_require_member_default`, `node_modules_commonjs_module_require`, `node_modules_commonjs_require_alias`, `node_modules_commonjs_require_side_effect`, `node_modules_commonjs_wrapper_globals`, `node_modules_commonjs_module_metadata`, `node_modules_commonjs_module_metadata_more`, `node_modules_commonjs_module_paths`. Still missing: arbitrary dynamic computed named-export metadata, broader runtime-computed object whole-value `module.exports = ...` expressions, deeper CommonJS wrapper behavior beyond this static `module.require(...)` subset, and mixed CJS/ESM interop edge cases. Dependency init stays eager through the AOT module graph by design.
  - Function-scoped static literal CommonJS `require("pkg")` destructuring supports default initializers for absent static exports while keeping present-export defaults unevaluated, and top-level/function-scoped static require destructuring rest bindings materialize remaining known named exports into dynamic objects. Tests: `node_modules_commonjs_require_destructure`, `node_modules_commonjs_function_scope_require`.
  - Direct declared-object CommonJS `module.exports = api` assignments are implemented for supported static object entries, including package-local require-backed values, with named import metadata and require-bound whole-object reads covered by `node_modules_commonjs_module_exports_object_identifier_named`.
  - CommonJS whole-value object chains such as `module.exports = exports.default = { ... }` and `exports.default = module.exports = { ... }` are implemented for supported static object-literal defaults, with named default metadata and require-bound whole-object reads covered by `node_modules_commonjs_module_exports_object_value_chain` and `node_modules_commonjs_module_exports_object_reverse_value_chain`.
  - Chained CommonJS object-literal `exports = module.exports = { ... }` and `module.exports = exports = { ... }` assignments are implemented for supported static object entries, with named import metadata and require-bound whole-object reads covered by `node_modules_commonjs_module_exports_object_chain_named` and `node_modules_commonjs_module_exports_object_reverse_chain_named`.
  - Direct CommonJS `module.exports = require("./local.js")` assignments and `exports = module.exports = require("./local.js")` chains are implemented for supported target `exports.*` metadata, with named import metadata and require-bound whole-object reads covered by `node_modules_commonjs_relative_require_object_named` and `node_modules_commonjs_relative_require_object_chain_named`.
  - CommonJS `const local = require("./local.js"); module.exports = local;` assignments are implemented for supported target `exports.*` metadata, with named import metadata and require-bound whole-object reads covered by `node_modules_commonjs_relative_require_binding_object_named`.
  - Basic `allowJs: true` package-source loading is implemented for pure ESM JavaScript packages; broader JS package patterns remain
  - Native addon package detection for literal imports/requires now rejects installed package roots containing `build/Release/*.node`, including transitive imports from emitted package sources under `node_modules`, unless the specifier is listed in a compile-time native-addon manifest. Manifest-listed literal require/import bindings lower to the embedded Node bridge with a concrete `.node` path instead of a runtime search; `bun run test:native-addon-smoke` builds and executes a real N-API addon through that bridge when `libnode` is available. Broader package export/imports/condition resolution remains.

- **Phase 15 — perf & polish** (ongoing)
  - Inline-caching stats and diagnostics
  - Basic escape analysis to stack-allocate objects that don't outlive their frame
  - Dead-code elimination on the generated C
  - Further binary-size optimization and CI matrix (Linux ✓, macOS, Windows later)
