## 4. Smaller missing pieces

Within-phase gaps that can be picked off individually without the big phase-level investments:

- Broader type guards / narrowing for deeper discriminated-union patterns. Basic user-defined type predicates over interface-shaped dynamic unions including negative predicate branches, basic literal-discriminant unions over interface-shaped dynamic objects including negative and compound literal checks, switch-based literal-discriminant narrowing over interface-shaped dynamic unions, nested dotted discriminants over dynamic interface fields, nullable pointer `typeof` guards such as `string | null` / `string | undefined`, dynamic `string | number | boolean` `typeof` guards, `in`-operator narrowing over interface-shaped unions, and `Array.isArray` type-predicate narrowing over unknown dynamic values are implemented. Tests include `discriminated_unions`, `discriminated_union_negative`, `discriminated_union_compound`, `discriminated_union_switch`, `discriminated_union_nested`, `custom_predicates`, `custom_predicates_negative`, `typeof_guards`, `typeof_boolean_union`, `in_operator_narrowing`, and `array_is_array_narrowing`.
- More complex generic type relationships. Direct top-level generic function calls, typed array callback references, concrete generic function-value adapters, erased generic classes, and generic instance/static method calls with concrete `T` / `T[]` specializations are implemented, including literal/const-literal computed generic method names, fixed-arity spread calls for generic functions/methods, erased generic class methods, erased generic class getter/setter accessors, and standard class decorator replacement constructors for erased generic classes including spread constructor calls and static `Reflect.construct` class targets. Tests: `generic_functions`, `generic_methods`, `generic_classes`, `generic_class_accessors`, `generic_class_decorator_replacement`, `generic_class_decorator_spread_replacement`, `generic_class_decorator_reflect_construct`.
- Explicit `this: void` function parameters are compile-time-only and do not add generated receiver arguments for direct calls, function-typed values, or higher-order callbacks. Test: `function_this_void`.
- Spread calls through direct fixed-arity function/namespace/method/constructor calls and first-class function values are implemented for typed-array, dynamic-array, and string argument sources where the final runtime arity matches the target signature, including standard class decorator replacement constructors for ordinary and erased generic classes; runtime arity mismatches throw catchable exceptions. Tests: `rest_spread`, `reflect_length_errors`, `namespaces`, `classes`, `generic_functions`, `generic_methods`, `function_value_spread`, `class_decorator_spread_replacement`, `generic_class_decorator_spread_replacement`.
- Literal, const-literal, and asserted non-literal static-expression computed class fields, methods, and accessors are implemented for instance and static members, with static field initializers and static blocks evaluated in member order during module init. Tests: `class_computed_members`, `class_computed_accessors`, `class_computed_nonliteral_members`, `class_static_blocks`.
- A narrow `Date` subset is implemented for `Date.now()` including evaluated ignored extra arguments, callable `Date(...)` evaluating and ignoring arguments before returning the current local Date string, `Date.UTC(year?, month?, ...)` with JavaScript optional-argument defaults and evaluated ignored arguments beyond the seventh date component, `Date.parse(text?, ...ignored)` over deterministic ISO strings with no-argument `NaN` and evaluated ignored extra arguments, `new Date()`, `new Date(ms)`, `new Date(text)`, `new Date(existingDate)`, `new Date(year, month, ...)` with evaluated extra numeric-constructor arguments ignored beyond the seventh date component, `.getTime()`, UTC component getters, local-time component getters, `.getYear()`, `.getTimezoneOffset()`, `.setTime(ms)`, legacy `.setYear(year)`, local-time mutators (`setFullYear`, `setMonth`, `setDate`, `setHours`, `setMinutes`, `setSeconds`, `setMilliseconds`) with invalid-receiver epoch rebuild for `setFullYear`, UTC mutators (`setUTCFullYear`, `setUTCMonth`, `setUTCDate`, `setUTCHours`, `setUTCMinutes`, `setUTCSeconds`, `setUTCMilliseconds`) with invalid-receiver epoch rebuild for `setUTCFullYear`, mutator methods evaluating then ignoring extra arguments beyond the fields JavaScript consumes, `.valueOf()`, local `.toString()` / `String(date)`, bounded en-US `.toLocaleString()`, `.toLocaleDateString()`, `.toLocaleTimeString()` with evaluated ignored locale/options arguments, `.toDateString()`, `.toTimeString()`, `.toISOString()` with invalid receivers throwing `RangeError: Invalid time value`, `.toUTCString()` / `.toGMTString()`, and `.toJSON(key?)` / extra arguments to zero-argument Date methods evaluating before being ignored where JavaScript ignores them; the ambient Date shim accepts those ignored arguments without `@ts-ignore`. Valid dates return UTC ISO strings from `toJSON(...)`; invalid dates return `null`. Tests: `date_now`, `date_callable`, `date_instances`, `date_locale_parts`, `date_local_constructor`, `date_legacy_year`, `date_local_setters`, `date_utc`, `date_parse`, `date_set_time`, `date_utc_getters`, `date_local_getters`, `date_utc_setters`, `date_to_date_string`, `date_to_time_string`, `date_to_iso_string`, `date_to_utc_string`, `date_to_json`, `date_to_json_invalid`, `date_ignored_arguments`.
- A narrow `Error` object subset is implemented for `new Error(message?, options?, ...ignored)`, callable `Error(message?, options?, ...ignored)`, and the same constructor/callable forms for `TypeError`, `RangeError`, `SyntaxError`, `ReferenceError`, `EvalError`, `URIError`, and `AggregateError`, covering `.name`, `.message`, literal `{ cause }` options exposed through `.cause`, `.toString(...ignored)`, `.toLocaleString(...ignored)`, `.valueOf(...ignored)`, evaluated ignored extra constructor/string/value method arguments, `AggregateError.errors`, and throw stringification through the existing exception channel. Tests: `error_instances`, `error_constructors`, `error_more_constructors`, `aggregate_error_constructor`, `error_cause`.
- `new Map(existingMap)` copy construction for typed Map sources is implemented. Test: `map_constructor_from_map`.
- ES2024 `Object.groupBy(items, keyFn)` returning a dynamic null-prototype object and `Map.groupBy(items, keyFn)` returning a typed `Map<K, T[]>` are implemented, including inline expression-body and single-return block-body callbacks plus explicit `this: any` callbacks receiving the JavaScript default `undefined` receiver. Tests: `object_group_by`, `map_group_by`, `group_by_this_param`.
- ES2025 Set composition methods (`union`, `intersection`, `difference`, `symmetricDifference`, `isSubsetOf`, `isSupersetOf`, `isDisjointFrom`) over `Set<T>` of matching element types are implemented. Test: `set_composition`.
- `new Set(existingSet)` copy construction for typed Set sources is implemented. Test: `set_constructor_from_set`.
- `Array.from(items, mapfn)` / `Array.from(items, mapfn, thisArg)` for typed array, typed `Map<string, V>` entry, typed Set, string code-point, and boxed dynamic array/string sources is implemented, including single-return block-body inline mapper callbacks and optional `thisArg` evaluation/binding for callbacks that declare `this: any`. Tests: `array_from_mapper`, `array_from_map`, `array_from_set`, `array_from_dynamic_mapper`, `array_from_mapper_this_arg`.
- `Array.from(set)` and `Array.from(set, mapfn)` for typed Set sources are implemented. Test: `array_from_set`.
- `Array.from(map)` for typed `Map<string, V>` sources is implemented, returning `ObjectEntry<V>[]` in insertion order. Test: `array_from_map`.
- `Object.fromEntries(map)` for typed `Map<string, V>` sources is implemented for contextual interface/class object targets. Test: `object_from_entries_map`.
- Interface `extends` is implemented for inherited interface fields, including multiple and nested base interfaces. Test: `interface_inheritance`.
- Custom iterator objects whose `next()` method is inherited from a base class are implemented for `for...of`. Test: `custom_iterator_inherited_next`.
- Custom iterators yielding `ObjectEntry<T>` values support `[key, value]` destructuring in `for...of`. Test: `custom_iterator_entry_destructure`.
- Typed numeric bitwise compound assignments are implemented. Test: `bitwise_assign`.
- Dynamic bitwise binary and compound assignments are implemented, including property and index lvalues. Test: `dynamic_bitwise_ops`.
- Dynamic unary numeric operators are implemented over `any` values. Test: `dynamic_unary_ops`.
- Dynamic pre/post update operators are implemented over local `any` variables plus dynamic property and index lvalues. Test: `dynamic_update_ops`.
- Dynamic `for...of` array-binding rest destructuring is implemented for boxed dynamic arrays. Test: `dynamic_for_of_rest`.
- The `void` operator is implemented with operand side-effect preservation. Test: `void_operator`.
- The comma operator is implemented with left-to-right side-effect preservation and right-hand value result. Test: `comma_operator`.
- Exponentiation compound assignment is implemented for typed number, BigInt, and dynamic values. Test: `exponent_assign`.
- Logical assignment is implemented with RHS short-circuiting for typed and dynamic lvalues. Test: `logical_assign`.
- Dynamic property/index exponent and logical assignment is implemented with descriptor-aware writes and RHS short-circuiting. Test: `dynamic_property_logical_assign`.
- `for (const k in expr)` enumeration over typed classes/interfaces, typed arrays, and dynamic `tsc_value_t` objects is implemented. Test: `for_in`.
- Typed `string +=` compound assignment is implemented. Test: `string_compound_plus`.
- Decorators — basic standard class decorator evaluation for named classes is implemented with dynamic `kind`/`name` context objects, including direct decorator functions, decorator-factory closure results, and dynamic callable/proxy-backed decorator functions; basic standard method, field, getter, and setter decorator evaluation is implemented for named instance/static members with dynamic `kind`/`name`/`static`/`private` context objects, plus shared dynamic `metadata` objects per decorated class and queued `addInitializer` callbacks that run after decorator evaluation during module initialization. Multiple decorator expressions on the same class or member evaluate top-down and invoke bottom-up, dynamic callable/proxy-backed decorator functions dispatch through `tsc_value_apply_function`, proxy-backed method decorators can return replacement functions through the dynamic decorator apply path, class decorators can return AOT constructor replacement functions for direct `new Class(...)`, parenthesized constructor targets, decorated class binding reads used as dynamic constructor values, and static `Reflect.construct(Class, args)` targets including spread constructor calls and erased generic class constructors, stacked class decorator replacements compose while forwarding constructor arguments through AOT replacement constructors, original class values passed to decorators can be constructed through `Reflect.construct(value, args)`, field decorators can return initializer replacement functions for instance and static field initial values with multiple returned initializers applied top-down, static method decorators can return replacement functions for direct `Class.method(...)` calls and can call the original static method through `Reflect.apply(value, undefined, args)`, instance method decorators can return replacement functions for direct `obj.method(...)` calls with the actual instance passed to typed class `this` receivers and can call the original method value through `Reflect.apply(value, this, args)`, static getter decorators can return replacement functions for direct `Class.property` reads and can call the original getter through `Reflect.apply(value, undefined, [])`, static setter decorators can return replacement functions for direct `Class.property = value` writes and can call the original setter through `Reflect.apply(value, undefined, [next])`, instance getter decorators can return replacement functions for direct `obj.property` reads with typed class `this` receivers and can call the original getter value through `Reflect.apply(value, this, [])`, and instance setter decorators can return replacement functions for direct `obj.property = value` writes with typed class `this` receivers and can call the original setter value through `Reflect.apply(value, this, [next])`. Literal, const-literal, and asserted non-literal static-expression computed member names are covered for field, method, getter, and setter decorators. Typed class getter/setter invocation is implemented for named instance/static accessors, including plain, numeric/string compound, and logical setter assignments. Still missing broader decorator replacement edge cases beyond the currently covered computed-name and erased-generic constructor forms. Tests: `class_decorator_basic`, `class_decorator_factory`, `class_decorator_replacement`, `class_decorator_dynamic_value_replacement`, `class_decorator_parenthesized_replacement`, `class_decorator_spread_replacement`, `class_decorator_reflect_construct`, `class_decorator_replacement_order`, `generic_class_decorator_replacement`, `generic_class_decorator_spread_replacement`, `generic_class_decorator_reflect_construct`, `method_decorator_basic`, `instance_method_decorator_replacement`, `instance_method_decorator_this_receiver`, `instance_method_decorator_original`, `static_method_decorator_replacement`, `static_decorator_originals`, `field_decorator_basic`, `field_decorator_initializer`, `field_decorator_initializer_order`, `decorator_computed_members`, `decorator_computed_nonliteral_members`, `accessor_decorator_basic`, `instance_getter_decorator_replacement`, `instance_getter_decorator_this_receiver`, `instance_getter_decorator_original`, `instance_setter_decorator_replacement`, `instance_setter_decorator_this_receiver`, `instance_setter_decorator_original`, `static_getter_decorator_replacement`, `static_setter_decorator_replacement`, `decorator_metadata_basic`, `decorator_add_initializer_basic`, `decorator_proxy_basic`, `decorator_proxy_replacement`, `decorator_replacement_order`, `decorator_factory_order`, `class_accessors_basic`, `class_accessors_compound`, `class_accessors_logical`.

---

## 5. AOT closure requirements

These are not permanent product limits, but every reachable module, native bridge, and runtime-compiled source must be closed over at build time. `tsc2c` should keep rejecting cases it cannot prove or list ahead of time.

- **Runtime code compilation.** Constant `eval(...)` expressions and constant-body `Function(...)` / `new Function(...)` calls compile AOT without `--unsafe-eval`, including forms with static parameter-name strings before the final body argument. Manifest-listed non-constant eval expressions and function bodies dispatch over the compile-time allow-list, whose entries may be arrays or named object maps; function manifest dispatch uses the final body argument when earlier parameter-name strings are static. Unknown source strings still require the gated embedded-Node bridge behind `--unsafe-eval`.
- **Dynamic `require(...)`.** Finite static proofs and `--dynamic-require-manifest` allow lists compile every listed specifier into the AOT module graph. Manifest `requires` entries may be either an array or a named object map, and unlisted non-finite require sites still reject.
- **Native C++ addons under `node_modules/*/build/Release/*.node`.** Literal native addon specifiers and native-addon packages can now be security allow-listed through a compile-time native-addon manifest, which lowers known `require(...)`/import bindings to `runtime/tsc_node_embed.cc` via `tsc_node_native_addon(<manifest path>)` and links `libnode`. Package `exports` / `imports` condition maps and package-private `#...` imports are included in the native-addon closure checks, direct `.node` default imports are typed as `any` for manifest-backed bridge imports, and `bun run test:native-addon-smoke` validates a real N-API addon path when `libnode` is available. Unlisted native addons still reject.

---

## How to pick

If the next session has **hours**, pick from section 4 (smaller pieces).

If it has **a few days to a week**, pick a bounded item from section 2, such as generator-backed iterables, unless the session is large enough to start Phase 3.

If it has **a week or more** to invest in one thing, do **Phase 3 (NaN-boxing)** from section 1. That one item unblocks about half of what's in sections 2–4.

If the goal is **"run a real npm package"**, the sequential chain is: Phase 3 → Closures → Phase 6 → Phase 14. Expect roughly two months of focused work for that end-to-end.

---

## File: `CHANGELOG.md`

# Changelog

All meaningful changes to `typescriptc` land here. Newest at the top.

## Unreleased

### Changed
- The e2e harness now materializes its small `node_modules` package fixtures before case discovery, so normal dependency installs no longer remove the ignored package-source fixtures needed by Phase 14 tests.
- Documentation drift sync: top-level `README.md` and `llms.txt` now reflect the current 822-passing test suite, ~43,100 LOC inventory, and full phase status including the implemented Proxy/Reflect surface, native-addon bridge path, AOT runtime-code compilation, dynamic-require manifests, and current Phase 14/decorator polish remaining work. `llms-full.txt` was regenerated from the updated source pages.
- The benchmark harness can now run the manual suite, generated operation-loop benchmarks for stdout-producing e2e cases via `--full` / `BENCH_SOURCE=e2e`, or both, records ops/sec in JSON/table output, and writes selectable JSON result files.
- Runtime and emitter hot paths for classes, typed object literals, string/number concatenation, JSON stringification, Map/Set, regex matching, arrays, and no-GC allocation were optimized for the benchmark suite.
- Crypto hashing now uses OpenSSL EVP digest APIs instead of deprecated `SHA*_Init` / `SHA*_Update` / `SHA*_Final` calls.

### Fixed
- Trapless array Proxy values now forward direct dynamic writes, `Reflect.set`, `Object.defineProperty`, `Reflect.defineProperty`, length updates, and deletes to their array targets. Test: `proxy_array_mutation_forward`.
- Trapless array Proxy values now forward `Object.isExtensible`, `Reflect.isExtensible`, and `Reflect.preventExtensions` to their array targets so prevented targets reject new index writes and definitions. Test: `proxy_array_extensibility_forward`.
- Trapless array Proxy values now forward `Object.seal`, `Object.freeze`, `Object.isSealed`, and `Object.isFrozen` to their array targets; matching sealed existing-index descriptor updates now succeed while frozen updates still fail. Test: `proxy_array_seal_freeze_forward`.
- Array-target Proxy `isExtensible` and `preventExtensions` traps now validate reported results against the array target's real extensibility state. Test: `proxy_array_extensibility_trap_invariants`.
- Array-target Proxy `ownKeys` traps now enforce array `length`, sealed index, and non-extensible exact-key invariants. Test: `proxy_array_ownkeys_invariants`.
- Array-target Proxy `getOwnPropertyDescriptor` traps now enforce non-configurable `length`, sealed-index, non-extensible, and frozen data-descriptor invariants. Test: `proxy_array_descriptor_invariants`.
- Array-target Proxy `defineProperty` traps now enforce non-extensible additions, new non-configurable keys, and frozen fixed-data update invariants. Test: `proxy_array_define_invariants`.
- Array-target Proxy `get` and `set` traps now enforce frozen index and frozen `length` fixed-data invariants while preserving sealed writable-index trap flexibility. Test: `proxy_array_get_set_invariants`.
- Array-target Proxy `has` and `deleteProperty` traps now enforce non-configurable `length`, sealed-index, and non-extensible key invariants. Test: `proxy_array_has_delete_invariants`.
- Typed arrays now track prototype state for `Object.getPrototypeOf`, `Object.setPrototypeOf`, `Reflect.getPrototypeOf`, and `Reflect.setPrototypeOf`, including non-extensible prototype-change rejection. Test: `array_prototypes`.
- Array-target Proxy `getPrototypeOf` and `setPrototypeOf` traps now forward to array targets and enforce non-extensible prototype invariants. Test: `proxy_array_prototype_invariants`.
- Boxed function identities now track prototype and extensibility state for Object/Reflect prototype helpers and non-extensible prototype-change rejection. Test: `function_prototypes`.
- Boxed function identities now track seal/freeze state, and trapless function Proxy values forward `Object.seal`, `Object.freeze`, `Object.isSealed`, and `Object.isFrozen` to their function targets. Test: `function_integrity`.
- Repeated direct references to the same function now reuse a stable boxed function identity, so `Object.is(fn as any, fn as any)` and shared function Object/Reflect integrity state behave consistently. Test: `function_integrity`.
- Boxed function identities now expose non-enumerable own `length` metadata through direct dynamic property reads, `Reflect.get`, `Object.hasOwn`, `Object.getOwnPropertyNames`, `Reflect.ownKeys`, and descriptor helpers; trapless function Proxy values forward the same length reads. Test: `function_integrity`.
- Boxed function identities now expose non-enumerable own `name` metadata through direct dynamic property reads, `Reflect.get`, own-key helpers, and descriptor helpers; trapless function Proxy values forward the same name reads. Test: `function_integrity`.
- Typed function values now route direct `Object.keys`/`values`/`entries`, own-key/descriptor helpers, prototype helpers, and extensibility/seal/freeze helpers through the boxed function-object path without requiring an `as any` cast. Test: `function_integrity`.
- Typed function values now route direct `Reflect.get`, `Reflect.has`, `Reflect.ownKeys`, `Reflect.getOwnPropertyDescriptor`, `Reflect.getPrototypeOf`, `Reflect.setPrototypeOf`, `Reflect.isExtensible`, and `Reflect.preventExtensions` through the boxed function-object path without requiring an `as any` cast. Test: `function_integrity`.
- Typed function metadata now respects non-configurable `length`/`name` descriptors for compatible `Object.defineProperty` / `Reflect.defineProperty` redefinitions and `Reflect.deleteProperty` refusal; direct `Object.defineProperty` works on typed function operands without `as any`. Test: `function_integrity`.
- Function-target Proxy `defineProperty` and `deleteProperty` traps now enforce non-configurable `length`/`name` metadata invariants. Test: `function_integrity`.
- Function-target Proxy `has` traps now enforce non-configurable `length`/`name` metadata invariants. Test: `function_integrity`.
- Function-target Proxy `ownKeys` coverage now includes extra-key rejection on non-extensible function targets. Test: `function_integrity`.
- Function-target Proxy `get`, `set`, `getOwnPropertyDescriptor`, and `ownKeys` traps now enforce non-configurable `length`/`name` metadata invariants. Test: `function_integrity`.
- Function-target Proxy `isExtensible` and `preventExtensions` traps now enforce target extensibility invariants. Test: `proxy_function_prototype_invariants`.
- Function-target Proxy `getPrototypeOf` and `setPrototypeOf` traps now forward to function targets and enforce non-extensible prototype invariants. Test: `proxy_function_prototype_invariants`.
- Proxy construct traps now have explicit coverage for returning arrays, functions, ordinary objects, and rejected primitive results. Test: `proxy_construct_return_objects`.
- Trapless array Proxy values now forward `Object.keys`, `Object.values`, `Object.entries`, `Reflect.ownKeys`, descriptor lookup, `Object.hasOwn`, `in`, and `propertyIsEnumerable` object-helper operations to their array targets. Test: `proxy_array_object_helpers`.
- `Object.prototype.toString.call(...)` now reports array Proxy chains as `[object Array]` and rejects revoked array proxy chains instead of tagging them as ordinary objects. Test: `proxy_array_to_string_tag`.
- `new Proxy(array, handler)` and `Proxy.revocable(array, handler)` now accept array targets, `Array.isArray(...)` follows direct and nested array proxy chains, dynamic array-proxy `.length` reads preserve the target length, and revoked array proxies throw through `Array.isArray(...)`. Test: `proxy_array_is_array`.
- `Object.prototype.toString.call(...)` now reports callable Proxy chains as `[object Function]` and rejects revoked callable proxy chains instead of tagging them as ordinary objects. Test: `proxy_callable_to_string_tag`.
- `Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(...)`, `propertyIsEnumerable.call(...)`, `isPrototypeOf.call(...)`, `toLocaleString.call(...)`, and `valueOf.call(...)` now reject nullish dynamic receivers after evaluating call arguments, while `Object.prototype.toString.call(...)` keeps the required nullish tags. Test: `object_prototype_nullish_call`.
- `JSON.parse(...)` syntax failures now throw through the catchable runtime exception path instead of aborting the process. Test: `json_parse_errors`.
- Static `Reflect.apply` / `Reflect.construct` and fixed-arity spread-call runtime arity mismatches now throw catchable runtime exceptions instead of aborting the process. Test: `reflect_length_errors`.
- `Number.prototype.toFixed`, `toExponential`, and `toPrecision` validation failures now throw catchable runtime exceptions for typed and dynamic receivers instead of aborting the process. Test: `number_format_errors`.
- `Number.prototype.toString(radix)` radix and bounded magnitude validation failures now throw catchable runtime exceptions for typed and dynamic receivers instead of aborting the process. Test: `number_to_string_errors`.
- `Array.prototype.with(...)` out-of-range failures now throw catchable runtime exceptions for typed and dynamic receivers instead of aborting the process. Test: `array_with_errors`.
- `String.fromCodePoint(...)` invalid-code-point failures now throw catchable runtime exceptions instead of aborting the process. Test: `string_from_code_point_errors`.
- `String.prototype.normalize(form)` invalid-form failures now throw catchable runtime exceptions for typed and dynamic receivers instead of aborting the process. Test: `string_normalize_errors`.
- BigInt constructor, division/modulo, exponentiation, and `toString(radix)` validation failures now throw catchable runtime exceptions instead of aborting the process. Test: `bigint_errors`.
- URL constructor/base-resolution and file-URL path validation failures now throw catchable runtime exceptions instead of aborting the process. Test: `url_errors`.
- Buffer encoding, size/length, offset, and swap validation failures now throw catchable runtime exceptions instead of aborting the process. Test: `buffer_errors`.
- Crypto algorithm, random byte size, and digest encoding validation failures now throw catchable runtime exceptions instead of aborting the process. Test: `crypto_errors`.
- `Object.create(...)` invalid prototype and dynamic `for...of` non-iterable failures now throw catchable runtime exceptions instead of aborting the process. Test: `dynamic_object_iteration_errors`.
- `child_process.execSync(...)` / `execFileSync(...)` command failure, timeout, and maxBuffer overflow now throw catchable runtime exceptions instead of aborting the process. Test: `child_process_sync_errors`.
- Unknown-source `eval` / `Function` diagnostics now describe the available AOT manifest and gated embedded-Node paths instead of implying an impossible runtime-code blocker.
- Documentation and agent indexes now describe native addons, runtime code compilation, and dynamic `require(...)` as AOT closure requirements rather than impossible blockers; README and LLM indexes no longer list Proxy or load-on-demand require execution as remaining targets.
- Inferred locals whose TypeScript type is erased to `tsc_value_t` now use boxed storage even when their initializer emits a narrower primitive, fixing nullish coalescing over `Map.get(...)` results and optional numeric field reads. Dynamic and typed string Reflect helpers again treat boxed strings as valid string-object targets. Tests: `nullish`, `wordcount`, `weak_ref`, `collection_object_methods`, `string_object_enumeration`, `dynamic_string_object_enumeration`.

### Added
- `Object.prototype.isPrototypeOf.call(...)` now compiles through the AOT call-form dispatch path for dynamic prototype chains and non-object false results while preserving ignored argument side effects. Test: `object_prototype_is_prototype_of_call`.
- `Object.prototype.valueOf.call(...)` now compiles through the AOT receiver-preserving dispatch path for typed objects, dynamic objects/arrays, typed arrays in typed contexts, and primitive receivers. Test: `object_prototype_value_of_call`.
- `Object.prototype.toLocaleString.call(...)` now compiles through an AOT dispatch path for typed objects, dynamic values, arrays, and primitive receivers. Test: `object_prototype_to_locale_string_call`.
- `Object.prototype.toString.call(...)` now compiles through an AOT tag dispatch path for typed receivers and a dynamic value tag helper for `any`/`unknown` receivers. Test: `object_prototype_to_string_call`.
- `Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(...)` and `Object.prototype.propertyIsEnumerable.call(...)` now compile through the AOT own-property dispatch path for typed objects, dynamic objects, arrays, strings, Buffers, and primitives. Test: `object_prototype_call`.
- `--runtime-code-manifest` now accepts named object-map allow lists for `eval` expressions and `Function` bodies in addition to arrays, compiling mapped source strings into the AOT dispatch path. Test: `runtime_code_manifest_object`.
- `--dynamic-require-manifest` now accepts named object-map allow lists in addition to array allow lists, compiling the mapped specifiers into the AOT module graph and runtime dispatch. Test: `dynamic_require_manifest_object`.
- The e2e harness now supports a per-case `compile.unsafe_eval` marker, and emit-C-only cases cover `--unsafe-eval` bridge emission for unknown-source `eval`, `Function`, and `new Function` without requiring `libnode` at test time. Tests: `runtime_eval_unsafe_bridge`, `runtime_function_unsafe_bridge`, `runtime_function_constructor_unsafe_bridge`.
- Constant-body `Function(...)` / `new Function(...)` calls now stay on the AOT path when they include static parameter-name strings, and runtime-code manifest dispatch uses the final function-body argument while requiring static parameter names. Tests: `runtime_function_params_aot`, `runtime_function_manifest_params`.
- Dynamic strict equality now preserves `null` and `undefined` literal identity when boxing values into `tsc_value_t`, including transparent asserted null/undefined expressions and missing dynamic object properties compared with `undefined`. Test: `dynamic_nullish_equality`.
- Explicit `this: void` function parameters are now treated as compile-time-only markers, so direct calls, function-typed values, and higher-order callbacks do not receive a generated receiver argument. Test: `function_this_void`.
- Math coverage now explicitly exercises `Math.atan2(...)` and `Math.random(...ignored)` range and ignored-argument behavior. Test: `math`.
- Bounded scheduler callbacks for `process.nextTick`, `queueMicrotask`, zero-delay `setTimeout`, and `setImmediate` now accept explicit `this: any` callback parameters and pass the runtime `undefined` value. Test: `scheduler_callback_this`.
- EventTarget listener adapters now support explicit `this: EventTarget` listener parameters, passing the dispatch target while preserving duplicate suppression, removal, and once-listener behavior. Test: `event_target_this`.
- EventEmitter listener adapters now support explicit `this: EventEmitter` listener parameters, passing the emitting instance for `on`/`once`/prepend variants while preserving listener identity filtering and removal. Test: `event_emitter_this`.
- Top-level and function-scoped static CommonJS `require("pkg")` destructuring now supports rest bindings by materializing the remaining known named exports into a dynamic object. Tests: `node_modules_commonjs_require_destructure`, `node_modules_commonjs_function_scope_require`.
- `os.userInfo(...)` now accepts literal UTF-8 option objects such as `{ encoding: "utf8" }` / `{ encoding: "utf-8" }` for the existing string-valued dynamic result subset. Test: `os_user_info`.
- `fs.readdirSync` and immediate `fs.promises.readdir` now accept literal `{ withFileTypes: true, recursive: true }` options and return recursive bounded `Dirent` results. Test: `fs_readdir_dirents`.
- Function-scoped literal CommonJS `require("pkg")` destructuring now supports default initializers for absent static exports while preserving present-export bindings without evaluating their defaults. Test: `node_modules_commonjs_function_scope_require`.
- Top-level literal CommonJS `require("pkg")` destructuring now supports default initializers for absent static exports while preserving present-export bindings without evaluating their defaults. Test: `node_modules_commonjs_require_destructure`.
- `fs.statSync`, `fs.lstatSync`, `fs.promises.stat`, and `fs.promises.lstat` now accept literal `{ throwIfNoEntry: false }`, returning `undefined` for missing paths instead of throwing or rejecting while preserving the existing `Stats` result for present paths. Test: `fs_stat_options`.
- Array-backed generator `.next(value)` calls now evaluate the optional input argument before advancing the materialized iterator, while still ignoring it in the eager generator subset. Test: `generator_next_argument`.
- `process.stdin.readable`, `process.stdout.writable`, and `process.stderr.writable` now expose stable boolean stream-state flags for the bounded stdio stream subset. Test: `process_stdio_readable_writable`.
- `process.stdin.fd` and `process.stdin.isTTY` now expose bounded readable-stream metadata alongside the existing stdout/stderr stream subset. Test: `process_stdin_metadata`.
- `process.stdout.fd`, `process.stderr.fd`, `process.stdout.isTTY`, and `process.stderr.isTTY` now expose bounded writable-stream metadata for the existing stdio subset. Test: `process_stdio_metadata`.
- `process.stdout.write(...)` and `process.stderr.write(...)` now accept optional encoding and zero-argument callback arguments in the existing synchronous stdio subset, evaluating encoding arguments before writing and invoking callbacks after string or Buffer writes. Tests: `process_stdio_write`, `process_stdio_write_buffer`, `process_stdio_write_callback`.
- Typed `Array.prototype.find()` and `findLast()` now return boxed `undefined` when no element matches for element types that can flow through `tsc_value_t`, and inferred numeric/boolean nullish locals keep boxed storage so assigned misses preserve `undefined` instead of collapsing to `NaN` or `false`. Tests: `array_hof`, `array_find_last`.
- Standard class decorator replacements now apply when decorated class bindings are read as dynamic constructor values and used through dynamic `new` or dynamic `Reflect.construct`. Test: `class_decorator_dynamic_value_replacement`.
- Standard class decorator replacements now apply to parenthesized constructor targets such as `new (Box)(...)` and parenthesized fixed-arity spread constructor calls. Test: `class_decorator_parenthesized_replacement`.
- Standard class decorator replacements now apply to static `Reflect.construct(Class, args)` targets for ordinary and erased generic classes across array-literal, array-literal-spread, typed-array, and dynamic-array argument lists. Tests: `class_decorator_reflect_construct`, `generic_class_decorator_reflect_construct`.
- Standard class decorator replacements now apply to fixed-arity spread constructor calls for ordinary and erased generic classes. Tests: `class_decorator_spread_replacement`, `generic_class_decorator_spread_replacement`.
- Standard class decorator replacements now apply to erased generic class constructor calls, so `new Box<T>(...)` uses the AOT replacement path instead of bypassing it. Test: `generic_class_decorator_replacement`.
- Proxy `getOwnPropertyDescriptor` result validation now rejects descriptor trap results that change the `enumerable` flag of a non-configurable target property. Test: `proxy_descriptor_invariants`.
- Proxy `getOwnPropertyDescriptor` result validation now rejects descriptor trap results that report a different getter or setter for a non-configurable accessor property. Test: `proxy_descriptor_invariants`.
- Proxy `defineProperty` result validation now rejects successful trap reports that would replace the getter or setter identity of a non-configurable accessor property. Test: `proxy_define_accessor`.
- Revoked callable Proxy values nested behind another proxy now preserve `typeof` identity while `String(...)` and `JSON.stringify(...)` report revoked-get errors through the proxy chain. Test: `proxy_nested_callable_identity`.
- Nested callable Proxy values now preserve callable identity through `typeof`, `String(...)`, `JSON.stringify(...)`, dynamic `Reflect.apply`, and dynamic `Reflect.construct`, including object-property omission and top-level/array `null` behavior for JSON. Test: `proxy_nested_callable_identity`.
- Proxy `defineProperty` handling now routes accessor descriptors through the proxy trap, validates non-callable accessor `defineProperty` traps, falls back to target accessor definition when the trap is absent, and rejects accessor additions/redefinitions that violate non-extensible or fixed-data target invariants. Test: `proxy_define_accessor`.
- Proxy object traps now reject non-callable `get`, `set`, `has`, `deleteProperty`, `defineProperty`, `getOwnPropertyDescriptor`, `ownKeys`, `getPrototypeOf`, `setPrototypeOf`, `isExtensible`, and `preventExtensions` trap values before dispatch while preserving callable proxy-valued trap forwarding. Test: `proxy_object_trap_callable_validation`.
- `Object.setPrototypeOf(dynamic, proto)` now rejects nullish targets, invalid prototype values, failed non-extensible updates, and falsy proxy `setPrototypeOf` trap results through catchable runtime errors while keeping primitive targets compatible. Test: `object_set_prototype_of_validation`.
- Dynamic object method calls now have focused coverage for callable Proxy property values, including `this` receiver binding, trapless forwarding, revoked-callable errors, and non-callable proxy target validation. Test: `proxy_method_call`.
- Dynamic `any` new expressions now dispatch through boxed constructable identities, including identifier and property-access constructor values, constructable Proxy values with `construct` traps, trapless forwarding, revoked-construct errors, and non-constructable proxy target validation. Test: `proxy_direct_construct`.
- Dynamic `any` call expressions now dispatch through boxed callable identities, including callable Proxy values with `apply` traps, trapless forwarding, revoked-callable errors, and non-callable proxy target validation. Test: `proxy_direct_call`.
- Dynamic `Reflect.get`, `Reflect.set`, `Reflect.has`, `Reflect.deleteProperty`, `Reflect.ownKeys`, `Reflect.defineProperty`, and `Reflect.getOwnPropertyDescriptor` now reject non-object dynamic targets through catchable runtime errors. Test: `reflect_property_target_validation`.
- Dynamic `Reflect.getPrototypeOf`, `Reflect.setPrototypeOf`, `Reflect.isExtensible`, and `Reflect.preventExtensions` now reject non-object dynamic targets through catchable runtime errors; `Reflect.setPrototypeOf` also rejects non-object/non-null prototypes. Test: `reflect_object_target_validation`.
- Dynamic `Reflect.apply` and `Reflect.construct` now accept object `ArrayLike` `argumentsList` values, normalizing them before function or proxy trap dispatch. Test: `reflect_arguments_array_like`.
- Dynamic `Reflect.construct(target, args, newTarget?)` now reports catchable target, argument-list, and newTarget validation errors before proxy construct trap dispatch. Test: `reflect_construct_validation`.
- Dynamic `Reflect.apply(target, thisArg, argumentsList)` now reports catchable target and argument-list validation errors, including rejecting invalid proxy apply argument lists before trap dispatch. Test: `reflect_apply_validation`.
- Dynamic `Reflect.construct(target, args, newTarget)` now validates that explicit `newTarget` values are constructable before dispatching function or proxy construction. Test: `reflect_construct_new_target_validation`.
- Proxy `apply` and `construct` paths now reject object-target proxies before trap dispatch, so handlers cannot make non-callable or non-constructable targets callable. Test: `proxy_callable_target_validation`.
- Proxy `ownKeys` trap validation now rejects non-string array entries through catchable runtime exceptions instead of coercing them to string keys. Test: `proxy_ownkeys_entry_validation`.
- Revoked callable Proxy values now preserve `typeof proxy === "function"` identity while `String(proxy)` and `JSON.stringify(proxy)` report revoked-get errors instead of silently treating the proxy as an ordinary object. Test: `proxy_revocable_identity`.
- Proxy `ownKeys` trap validation now rejects non-array trap results for both `Reflect.ownKeys(proxy)` and `Object.keys(proxy)` through catchable runtime exceptions. Test: `proxy_ownkeys_result_validation`.
- Dynamic `Reflect.construct(target, args, newTarget)` now accepts an explicit `newTarget` for dynamic targets and passes it through proxy construct traps by identity. Test: `proxy_construct_new_target`.
- Proxy `apply` and `construct` trap validation now reports non-callable traps and primitive construct-trap results through catchable runtime exceptions instead of the generic panic path. Test: `proxy_callable_trap_validation`.
- Proxy construction now reports invalid non-object targets or handlers through the catchable runtime exception path instead of aborting, covering `new Proxy(...)` and `Proxy.revocable(...)`. Test: `proxy_constructor_validation`.
- Callable Proxy values without an `apply` trap now have focused coverage for forwarding `Reflect.apply(proxy, thisArg, args)` to function targets while preserving the supplied receiver and argument list. Test: `proxy_apply_forward`.
- Revocable callable and constructable Proxy values now have focused coverage for throwing on `Reflect.apply` and `Reflect.construct` after revocation. Test: `proxy_revocable_callable`.
- Constructable Proxy values without a `construct` trap now have focused coverage for forwarding `Reflect.construct(proxy, args)` to function targets, including dynamic receiver initialization and explicit object returns. Test: `proxy_construct_forward`.
- Dynamic `Reflect.construct(functionValue, args)` now constructs boxed generic function identities with a dynamic `this` receiver, returning explicit object results or the initialized receiver when the constructor returns a primitive. Test: `reflect_construct_dynamic_function`.
- Callable Proxy values over function targets now follow dynamic function JSON behavior: object properties are omitted and array/top-level slots stringify as `null` in the existing runtime model. Test: `proxy_callable_json`.
- `JSON.parse(...)` now decodes `\uXXXX` string escapes, including surrogate pairs emitted as UTF-8 runtime strings. Test: `dynamic_values`.
- Callable Proxy values over function targets now preserve function stringification through dynamic `String(proxy)` / `toString` coercion while ordinary object proxies still stringify as objects. Test: `proxy_callable_string`.
- Callable and constructable Proxy values now preserve JavaScript `typeof proxy === "function"` identity when the proxy target is a function. Test: `proxy_callable_identity`.
- Negative user-defined type predicate branches now have focused coverage for narrowing interface-shaped dynamic unions. Test: `custom_predicates_negative`.
- Compound literal discriminant checks using `||` and `&&` now have focused coverage for narrowing interface-shaped dynamic unions. Test: `discriminated_union_compound`.
- Proxy-backed standard method decorators now have focused coverage for returning replacement functions that dispatch through the dynamic decorator apply path. Test: `decorator_proxy_replacement`.
- Static standard method/getter/setter decorator replacements now have focused coverage for calling the original static member value through `Reflect.apply(value, undefined, args)`. Test: `static_decorator_originals`.
- Stacked standard class decorator replacements now compose in bottom-up invocation order while forwarding constructor arguments through AOT replacement constructors. Test: `class_decorator_replacement_order`.
- Asserted non-literal static expressions now resolve as ordinary computed class field, method, and accessor names. Test: `class_computed_nonliteral_members`.
- Asserted non-literal static expressions such as `("ta" + "g") as "tag"` now resolve as computed class member names for standard field, method, getter, and setter decorators. Test: `decorator_computed_nonliteral_members`.
- Literal and const-literal computed standard class member names now have focused decorator coverage across field initializer replacements, method replacements, and getter/setter replacements. Test: `decorator_computed_members`.
- Standard class decorator replacements can now return AOT constructor functions used by direct `new Class(...)` calls; the original class value passed to decorators is constructible through `Reflect.construct(value, args)`. Broader replacement edge cases remain deferred. Test: `class_decorator_replacement`.
- Instance standard setter decorator replacement functions can now call the original setter value with `Reflect.apply(value, this, [next])`, with the boxed receiver bridged back to the typed class instance. Test: `instance_setter_decorator_original`.
- Instance standard getter decorator replacement functions can now call the original getter value with `Reflect.apply(value, this, [])`, with the boxed receiver bridged back to the typed class instance. Test: `instance_getter_decorator_original`.
- Instance standard method decorator replacement functions can now call the original method value with `Reflect.apply(value, this, args)`, with the boxed receiver bridged back to the typed class instance. Test: `instance_method_decorator_original`.
- Instance standard setter decorator replacements can now declare a typed class `this` receiver; the emitted write passes the actual instance into the replacement. Test: `instance_setter_decorator_this_receiver`.
- Instance standard getter decorator replacements can now declare a typed class `this` receiver; the emitted read passes the actual instance into the replacement. Test: `instance_getter_decorator_this_receiver`.
- Instance standard method decorator replacements can now declare a typed class `this` receiver; the emitted call passes the actual instance into the replacement. Test: `instance_method_decorator_this_receiver`.
- Multiple standard field decorators now apply returned initializer functions in standard top-down order after bottom-up decorator invocation. Test: `field_decorator_initializer_order`.
- Standard decorator factory expressions now evaluate top-down before decorators invoke bottom-up, preserving standard side-effect ordering for multiple decorators. Test: `decorator_factory_order`.
- Multiple standard decorators on the same class or member now invoke bottom-up, so replacement functions compose in standard decorator order. Test: `decorator_replacement_order`.
- Instance standard setter decorators can now return replacement setter functions used by direct `obj.property = value` writes. Test: `instance_setter_decorator_replacement`.

- Static standard method decorators can now return replacement functions used by direct `Class.method(...)` calls. Test: `static_method_decorator_replacement`.
- Standard field decorators can now return initializer functions that transform instance and static field initial values during class initialization. Test: `field_decorator_initializer`.
- Dynamic callable and proxy-backed standard class/member decorator functions now dispatch through the boxed function/proxy apply path during module initialization. Test: `decorator_proxy_basic`.
- Standard decorator contexts now expose `addInitializer`; queued callbacks run after member and class decorator evaluation during module initialization. Test: `decorator_add_initializer_basic`.
- Erased generic class getter and setter accessors now have focused coverage for typed coercion at property read/write boundaries. Test: `generic_class_accessors`.
- Negative literal discriminant checks such as `kind !== "circle"` now have focused coverage for narrowing interface-shaped dynamic unions. Test: `discriminated_union_negative`.
- Literal and const-literal computed class getter and setter accessors are now covered alongside computed fields and methods. Test: `class_computed_accessors`.
- Standard decorator contexts now expose a shared dynamic `metadata` object for all decorators on a named class during module initialization. Test: `decorator_metadata_basic`.
- Typed class getter/setter accessor assignments now support logical assignment operators by reading through the getter, conditionally writing through the setter, and returning the JavaScript assignment result. Test: `class_accessors_logical`.
- Typed class getter/setter accessor assignments now support numeric and string compound assignment operators by reading through the getter, writing through the setter, and returning the assigned value. Test: `class_accessors_compound`.
- Typed class getter and setter accessors now lower to C calls for named instance and static accessors, including assignment-expression return values for plain setter assignments. Test: `class_accessors_basic`.
- Standard class decorators now evaluate during module initialization for named classes, with direct decorator functions and decorator-factory closure results receiving a dynamic context object containing `kind: "class"` and `name`. Broader class replacement edge cases remain deferred. Tests: `class_decorator_basic`, `class_decorator_factory`.
- Standard method decorators now evaluate during module initialization for named instance and static methods, with direct decorator functions receiving dynamic context objects containing `kind`, `name`, `static`, and `private`. Broader method replacement remains deferred. Test: `method_decorator_basic`.
- Standard field decorators now evaluate during module initialization for named instance and static fields, with direct decorator functions receiving dynamic context objects containing `kind`, `name`, `static`, and `private`. Test: `field_decorator_basic`.
- Standard getter and setter decorators now evaluate during module initialization for named instance and static accessors, with direct decorator functions receiving dynamic context objects containing `kind`, `name`, `static`, and `private`. Broader accessor replacement remains deferred. Test: `accessor_decorator_basic`.
- `Object.groupBy` and `Map.groupBy` callbacks that declare `this: any` now receive the JavaScript default `undefined` receiver across direct and inline callbacks. Test: `group_by_this_param`.

- Typed and dynamic array higher-order methods now accept optional `thisArg` values, evaluate them once, and bind them for callbacks that declare `this: any`. Test: `array_hof_this_arg`.
- CommonJS `require(...)` package edges now include the `node-addons` condition while resolving package `exports` and package-private `imports` condition maps into the AOT module graph, preferring it before `require` fallback when package order selects it. Test: `node_modules_package_require_node_addons_conditions`.
- Package source imports now include Node's `node-addons` condition ahead of `node`, so ESM import edges can select `node-addons` package `exports` / package-private `imports` branches before fallback conditions. Test: `node_modules_package_import_node_addons_conditions`.

- JavaScript package sources now have focused coverage for re-export barrels that forward named exports, default export aliases, and export-star bindings. Test: `node_modules_js_package_re_exports`.
- CommonJS `require(...)` package edges now have focused coverage for wildcard package `exports` and package-private `imports` condition maps, including `*` substitution into selected CommonJS source paths. Test: `node_modules_package_require_pattern_conditions`.
- CommonJS `require(...)` package edges now have focused coverage for package `exports` and package-private `imports` condition arrays, falling back from missing targets to the next valid AOT source. Test: `node_modules_package_require_array_conditions`.
- Package source resolution now tracks import and CommonJS require edges separately, so the same conditional package specifier can select an ESM import branch and a CommonJS require branch in one AOT entry. Test: `node_modules_package_dual_cjs_esm_resolution`.
- CommonJS `require(...)` package edges now resolve package `exports` and package-private `imports` condition maps through `require` branches while building the AOT module graph. Test: `node_modules_package_require_conditions`.
- Package source resolution now has focused coverage for package `exports` and package-private `imports` condition maps selecting `import` branches into the AOT module graph. Test: `node_modules_package_conditional_exports`.
- Native addon bridge smoke coverage now lives behind `bun run test:native-addon-smoke`: it builds a tiny N-API `.node` addon, compiles an allow-listed import through the embedded Node bridge, and verifies exported object properties when `libnode` is available. The embedded bridge now initializes a Node environment, captures `require`, and converts V8 object own properties into `tsc_value_t` objects.
- CommonJS whole-value object chains such as `module.exports = exports.default = { ... }` and `exports.default = module.exports = { ... }` now assign `exports.default` to the same emitted static object used for default imports and require-bound whole-object reads. Tests: `node_modules_commonjs_module_exports_object_value_chain`, `node_modules_commonjs_module_exports_object_reverse_value_chain`.
- CommonJS chained object-literal assignments such as `exports = module.exports = { ... }` and `module.exports = exports = { ... }` now expose static named metadata and require-bound whole-object reads. Tests: `node_modules_commonjs_module_exports_object_chain_named`, `node_modules_commonjs_module_exports_object_reverse_chain_named`.
- CommonJS `const local = require("./local.js"); module.exports = local;` re-exports now expose the target module's static named metadata and require-bound whole-object reads when the target uses supported `exports.*` assignments. Test: `node_modules_commonjs_relative_require_binding_object_named`.
- CommonJS `exports = module.exports = require("./local.js")` re-export chains now have focused coverage for the same static named metadata and require-bound whole-object reads as direct `module.exports = require(...)`. Test: `node_modules_commonjs_relative_require_object_chain_named`.
- CommonJS `module.exports = require("./local.js")` re-exports now expose the target module's static named metadata and require-bound whole-object reads when the target uses supported `exports.*` assignments. Test: `node_modules_commonjs_relative_require_object_named`.
- CommonJS package sources now expose static named metadata and require-bound whole-object reads for direct declared-object assignments such as `const api = { ... }; module.exports = api;`. Test: `node_modules_commonjs_module_exports_object_identifier_named`.
- CommonJS require bindings now preserve emitted runtime-computed whole `module.exports` objects for dynamic key reads, covering `module.exports = Object.fromEntries(...)` sources whose keys are not statically knowable as named export metadata. Test: `node_modules_commonjs_module_exports_dynamic_computed`.
- Native addon closure checks now include package `imports` maps and package-private `#...` import specifiers, direct `.node` default imports have an ambient `any` declaration, and direct `.node` imports can be allow-listed into the embedded-Node bridge path. Tests: `native_addon_manifest_import`, `native_addon_package_imports`.
- `--runtime-code-manifest <path>` now accepts explicit compile-time runtime-code allow-lists with JSON shape `{ "eval": ["1 + 2"], "functions": ["return 42;"] }`; listed non-constant source strings dispatch to generated AOT constants without enabling `--unsafe-eval`, while runtime values outside the allow-list throw instead of loading code dynamically. Tests: `runtime_eval_manifest`, `runtime_function_manifest`.
- Constant runtime-code strings now compile AOT for expression `eval("...")` and constant-body `Function("return ...")` / `new Function("return ...")` without enabling `--unsafe-eval`; non-static sources still reject unless unsafe eval is explicitly enabled. Tests: `runtime_eval`, `runtime_function_call`, `runtime_function_constructor`, `runtime_eval_unknown`, `runtime_function_call_unknown`, `runtime_function_constructor_unknown`.

- Dynamic `require(name)` finite specifier proofs now include computed static keys in top-level const string maps, so `require(table[key])` can enter the AOT graph even when the map is declared with keys such as `[key]` or `` [`${key}`] ``. Test: `dynamic_require_static_computed_map`.
- Dynamic `require(name)` finite specifier proofs now include top-level const string maps and arrays, so `require(table[key])` and `require(list[index])` can enter the AOT graph when every possible collection value is a static string. Test: `dynamic_require_static_collections`.
- Dynamic `require(name)` finite specifier proofs now include identifiers annotated as string-literal unions, including function parameters and top-level variables, so those alternatives enter the AOT module graph and runtime finite dispatch. Test: `dynamic_require_literal_union`.
- `--dynamic-require-manifest <path>` now accepts explicit compile-time finite dynamic `require(variable)` allow-lists with JSON shape `{ "requires": ["./specifier"] }`; allow-listed specifiers are compiled into the AOT module graph and value-returning calls dispatch over that finite set at runtime. Test: `dynamic_require_manifest`.
- Value-returning dynamic `require(name)` finite dispatch now also materializes AOT-known CommonJS named exports into a dynamic object for modules that assign `module.exports.name = ...`. Test: `dynamic_require`.

- Side-effect-only dynamic `require(name)` statements now collect finite conditional specifier alternatives into the AOT module graph while still rejecting non-finite variables and value-returning finite-set requires. Test: `dynamic_require`.
- Dynamic `require(name)` specifier proofs now include finite top-level const string concatenation and template expressions, so those edges enter the AOT module graph instead of requiring runtime loading. Test: `dynamic_require`.
- Proxy `getOwnPropertyDescriptor` trap results now enforce descriptor object/undefined returns, non-configurable target keys, non-extensible target keys, descriptor-kind consistency, and fixed-data value invariants. Test: `proxy_descriptor_invariants`.

- `--unsafe-eval` now gates runtime code compilation behind an embedded Node bridge: default `eval` / `Function` / `new Function` diagnostics remain hard failures, while the explicit flag emits `tsc_node_eval` / callable `tsc_node_function` bridge calls and links `runtime/tsc_node_embed.cc` only when `libnode` inputs are available. Focused checks cover default rejection, `--unsafe-eval --emit-c-only` bridge emission, callable `Function` bridge emission, and the local missing-`libnode` link diagnostic.

- `child_process.spawnSync(..., { encoding: "utf8", stdio: [...] })` now honors tuple stdin modes: `"pipe"` forwards `input` or EOF, while `"ignore"` routes stdin from `/dev/null`. Test: `child_process_spawn_sync_stdio_stdin`.
- `child_process.exec(...)` and `execFile(...)` callback option declarations now accept explicit UTF-8 `encoding` values. Test: `child_process_exec_callback_encoding`.
- `child_process.execFile(...)`, `execFileSync(...)`, and `spawnSync(...)` now have explicit coverage for literal `shell: false` direct `execvp` routing. Test: `child_process_shell_false`.
- `child_process.execSync(...)` and `execFileSync(...)` now accept explicit `encoding: "buffer"` options and keep returning Buffer output. Test: `child_process_exec_sync_buffer_encoding`.
- `child_process.spawnSync(..., { encoding: "utf8", stdio })` now accepts literal `"inherit"` and tuple entries that inherit stdout/stderr from the parent process. Test: `child_process_spawn_sync_stdio_inherit`.
- Child process sync, immediate-callback, and `spawnSync` subsets now accept numeric `maxBuffer`; callback and `spawnSync` overflows report `ENOBUFS` with truncated captured output, sync overflows throw catchable runtime exceptions. Test: `child_process_max_buffer_options`, `child_process_sync_errors`.
- `child_process.execFile(...)`, `execFileSync(...)`, and `spawnSync(...)` option declarations now accept POSIX-inert `windowsVerbatimArguments`. Test: `child_process_windows_verbatim_option`.
- Child process sync and immediate-callback subsets now apply POSIX `uid` / `gid` options in the child before `execvp`. Test: `child_process_uid_gid_options`.
- Child process sync and immediate-callback option declarations now accept POSIX-inert `windowsHide` for portable Node call sites. Test: `child_process_windows_hide_option`.
- `child_process.spawnSync(...)`, `execFileSync(...)`, and immediate `execFile(...)` now pass literal `argv0` through to the child process. Test: `child_process_argv0_options`.
- `child_process.spawnSync(..., { encoding: "utf8", stdio })` now accepts literal `"ignore"` and tuple `"pipe"` / `"ignore"` forms, returning `null` for ignored stdout/stderr result fields. Test: `child_process_spawn_sync_stdio_ignore`.
- `child_process.execSync(...)` and `execFileSync(...)` now accept numeric `timeout` plus literal `killSignal` options in the synchronous subset. Test: `child_process_exec_sync_timeout_options`.
- `child_process.execFileSync(...)` now drains child stderr internally while preserving stdout-only return values. Test: `child_process_exec_file_sync_stderr_pipe`.
- `child_process.exec(...)` and `execFile(...)` immediate callbacks now support bounded `timeout` / `killSignal` options and report `ETIMEDOUT`. Test: `child_process_exec_callback_timeout`.
- `child_process.spawnSync(..., { timeout, killSignal: "SIGKILL" })` now uses the requested bounded timeout signal. Test: `child_process_spawn_sync_kill_signal`.
- `child_process.spawnSync(..., { timeout })` now terminates timed-out children with `SIGTERM` and reports `error: "ETIMEDOUT"`. Test: `child_process_spawn_sync_timeout`.
- `child_process.exec` and `execSync` now accept literal shell path strings such as `{ shell: "/bin/sh" }`. Test: `child_process_exec_shell_string`.
- `child_process.spawnSync(..., { encoding: "utf8" })` now accepts explicit pipe-only `stdio` option forms. Test: `child_process_spawn_sync_stdio_pipe`.
- `child_process.execFile`, `execFileSync`, and `spawnSync` now accept literal shell path strings such as `{ shell: "/bin/sh" }` in addition to `shell: true`. Test: `child_process_shell_string`.
- `child_process.exec(...)` immediate callbacks now receive child setup error-code strings such as `ENOENT` for failures like invalid `cwd`. Test: `child_process_exec_callback_error`.
- `child_process.execFile(...)` immediate callbacks now receive child setup error-code strings such as `ENOENT` instead of treating `status: null` as success. Test: `child_process_exec_file_callback_error`.
- `child_process.execFile(file, callback)` now works for the immediate UTF-8 callback subset when no args array is needed. Test: `child_process_exec_file_callback_no_args`.
- `child_process.execFile(..., { shell: true })` and `execFileSync(..., { shell: true })` now route through the synchronous shell-backed subset. Test: `child_process_exec_file_shell`.
- `child_process.spawnSync(..., { shell: true, encoding: "utf8" })` now routes the synchronous UTF-8 subset through `/bin/sh -c` while preserving `cwd`, `env`, and `input`. Test: `child_process_spawn_sync_shell`.
- `child_process.execFile(file, options, callback)` and `spawnSync(file, options)` now accept the options object as the second argument when no args array is needed. Test: `child_process_options_second_arg`.
- `child_process.execFileSync(file, options)` now accepts the options object as the second argument when no args array is needed. Test: `child_process_exec_file_sync_options_second_arg`.
- `child_process` sync and immediate-callback subsets now accept literal string `env` option objects as child environment overlays. Test: `child_process_env_options`.
- `child_process.spawnSync(..., { encoding: "utf8" })` now reports `execvp`/child setup failures through the result `error` field instead of treating them as ordinary exit code 127 results. Test: `child_process_spawn_sync_exec_error`.
- `child_process.spawnSync(..., { encoding: "utf8" })` now reports signal termination with `status: null` and a signal name such as `SIGTERM`. Test: `child_process_spawn_sync_signal`.
- `child_process.spawnSync(..., { encoding: "utf8" })` now preserves nonzero child exit statuses in the result object without throwing. Test: `child_process_spawn_sync_nonzero_status`.
- `child_process.spawnSync(..., { encoding: "utf8" })` results now include successful-process metadata fields `pid`, `output`, `signal`, and `error` alongside `status`, `stdout`, and `stderr`. Test: `child_process_spawn_sync_result_metadata`.
- `child_process.execSync(..., { encoding: "utf8" })` and `execFileSync(..., { encoding: "utf8" })` now return UTF-8 strings instead of Buffers in the synchronous subset. Test: `child_process_exec_sync_encoding`.
- `child_process.exec(command, { cwd }, callback)` and `execFile(file, args, { cwd }, callback)` now run immediate UTF-8 callbacks in the requested working directory. Test: `child_process_exec_callbacks_cwd`.

- `child_process.spawnSync(..., { input })` now writes UTF-8 stdin for the synchronous UTF-8 subset. Test: `child_process_spawn_sync_input`.
- `child_process.execFileSync(file, args, { cwd })` now runs the child in the requested working directory. Test: `child_process_exec_file_sync_cwd`.
- `child_process.spawnSync(..., { cwd })` now runs the child in the requested working directory for the UTF-8 subset. Test: `child_process_spawn_sync_cwd`.

- `child_process.spawnSync(file, args, { encoding: "utf8" })` now captures synchronous stdout/stderr strings and exit status. Test: `child_process_spawn_sync`.
- `child_process.execFileSync(file, args?)` now executes a binary with argv synchronously and returns stdout as a Buffer. Test: `child_process_exec_file_sync`.

- `crypto.randomUUID()` now returns RFC 4122 version 4 UUID strings for global and named crypto imports. Test: `crypto_random_uuid`.
- `crypto.randomBytes(size)` now returns a random Buffer for global, named, and namespace crypto imports. Test: `crypto_random_bytes`.
- `Buffer` now supports float and double read/write helpers in little- and big-endian forms. Test: `buffer_float_io`.
- Global `btoa(...)` and `atob(...)` now provide byte-string base64 encode/decode helpers. Test: `base64_globals`.
- `Buffer.prototype.toJSON()` now returns the standard dynamic `{ type: "Buffer", data: [...] }` shape. Test: `buffer_to_json`.
- `Hash.digest("base64")` now emits base64 digests for supported crypto hashes. Test: `crypto_digest_base64`.
- `Buffer.from`, `Buffer.toString`, `Buffer.byteLength`, and `Buffer.isEncoding` now support `"base64"`. Test: `buffer_base64`.
- `Buffer.prototype.swap16()`, `swap32()`, and `swap64()` now mutate byte order in place and return the receiver. Test: `buffer_swap`.
- `Buffer` now supports signed 8/16/32-bit integer read/write helpers in little- and big-endian forms. Test: `buffer_int_io`.
- `Buffer` now supports unsigned 16/32-bit integer read/write helpers in little- and big-endian forms. Test: `buffer_uint_multi_io`.

- `Buffer.allocUnsafe(size)` and `Buffer.allocUnsafeSlow(size)` now route to deterministic Buffer allocation. Test: `buffer_alloc_unsafe`.
- `process.version` and `process.versions` now expose basic runtime compatibility metadata. Test: `process_versions`.

- `createHash` now routes from named and namespace imports from `"crypto"` / `"node:crypto"`. Test: `crypto_import`.
- `Buffer.prototype.indexOf`, `lastIndexOf`, and `includes` now accept string and Buffer needles in addition to numeric bytes. Test: `buffer_search_more`.

- `process.argv0`, `process.execPath`, and empty `process.execArgv` metadata are now exposed from the bootstrapped argv state. Test: `process_argv_meta`.
- `process.umask(mask?)` now reads or updates the native process file mode creation mask and returns the previous/current mask. Test: `process_umask`.
- `Buffer.concat(list, totalLength?)` now supports explicit output length with truncation or zero padding. Test: `buffer_concat_length`.
- `Buffer.from(existingBuffer)` now creates an independent byte copy. Test: `buffer_from_buffer`.

- `process.chdir(directory)` now changes the native process working directory and `process.cwd()` reflects the update. Test: `process_chdir`.
- POSIX process identity helpers `process.getuid()`, `process.getgid()`, `process.geteuid()`, and `process.getegid()` now lower to libc ID lookups. Test: `process_posix_ids`.
- `os.availableParallelism()`, `os.machine()`, and `os.version()` now expose host CPU and uname metadata through global `os`, namespace imports, and named imports. Test: `os_host_more`.

- `URL.canParse(input)` now checks whether the supported absolute `scheme://authority` URL subset can be constructed without throwing. Test: `url_can_parse`.

- `Buffer.prototype.copy(target[, targetStart[, sourceStart[, sourceEnd]]])` now copies clipped byte ranges into target Buffers and returns the copied byte count. Test: `buffer_copy`.
- `Buffer.prototype.fill(value[, start[, end]])` now mutates and returns Buffers for numeric byte fills with JS-style clipped indexes. Test: `buffer_fill`.

- `fs.constants.COPYFILE_EXCL`, `COPYFILE_FICLONE`, and `COPYFILE_FICLONE_FORCE` are now exposed, and `copyFileSync` / immediate `fs.promises.copyFile` accept optional flags with `COPYFILE_EXCL` no-overwrite enforcement. Test: `fs_copy_flags`.
- `path.posix.*` and named `posix` imports from `"path"` / `"node:path"` now route to the supported POSIX path subset, including `sep` and `delimiter`. Test: `path_posix`.
- `process.hrtime([previous])` now returns a synchronous monotonic `[seconds, nanoseconds]` pair and supports elapsed-time diffs. Test: `process_hrtime`.

- Date instances now support UTC mutator methods (`setUTCFullYear`, `setUTCMonth`, `setUTCDate`, `setUTCHours`, `setUTCMinutes`, `setUTCSeconds`, `setUTCMilliseconds`) with timestamp return values and normalized overflow. Test: `date_utc_setters`.
- Added POSIX `path.parse(path)` and `path.format(pathObject)` support for global, namespace, and named imports, using dynamic objects for parsed path records. Test: `path_parse_format`.

- Date instances now support `.setTime(ms)` mutation, and `new Date(existingDate)` copies the source timestamp. Test: `date_set_time`.
- `Date.parse(text)` and `new Date(text)` now support a bounded deterministic ISO subset: date-only strings, UTC `Z` timestamps, and numeric timezone offsets, returning `NaN` for unsupported input. Test: `date_parse`.

- `await` inside the immediate async subset now accepts non-Promise values, evaluating the operand once and continuing with the value immediately. Test: `async_await_values_immediate`.
- `dns.promises.lookup(hostname[, { family }])` now has an immediate-settled Promise subset for global `dns.promises`, named `promises` imports, and namespace imports from `"dns"` / `"node:dns"`, returning a dynamic `{ address, family }` object or a rejected Promise on lookup failure. Test: `dns_promises_lookup`.

- `dns.lookup(hostname, callback)` and `dns.lookup(hostname, { family }, callback)` now have an immediate callback subset for global `dns`, named imports, and namespace imports from `"dns"` / `"node:dns"`, backed by host `getaddrinfo` and returning address plus IPv4/IPv6 family. Tests: `dns_lookup`, `dns_lookup_options`.
- Local `try`/`catch` inside the immediate async subset now catches rejected native Promise records from `await`, while uncaught awaited rejections still return rejected Promise records. Test: `async_await_try_catch`.
- `await` inside the immediate async subset now unwraps fulfilled native Promise records, returns rejected Promise records for rejected awaits, and short-circuits pending awaits to pending without scheduling a continuation. Test: `async_await_immediate`.
- Top-level `async function` declarations, class `async` methods, and async function values without `await` now lower to immediate Promise records: returned values fulfill, returned native Promise records are adopted, implicit returns fulfill with `undefined`, and synchronous uncaught throws reject. Tests: `async_function_immediate`, `async_methods_immediate`, `async_function_values_immediate`, `async_throw_rejection`.
- `Error`, `TypeError`, `RangeError`, `SyntaxError`, `ReferenceError`, `EvalError`, `URIError`, and `AggregateError` now have a narrow object subset for constructor/callable forms, exposing `.name`, `.message`, `.toString()`, `.toLocaleString()`, and `.valueOf()`. `AggregateError` stores `.errors`, while `throw` still stringifies errors to the existing exception channel. Tests: `error_instances`, `error_constructors`, `error_more_constructors`, `aggregate_error_constructor`.
- `Date` now has a narrow instance subset: `new Date()`, `new Date(ms)`, `.getTime()`, `.valueOf()`, `.toString()`, and `.toLocaleString()` over millisecond timestamps. Test: `date_instances`.
